extracted.intended_audience: readers of The Spectator; literate early-18th-century public interested in manners, morals, and conduct
extracted.subtask_description: Short periodical essays (The Spectator) offering prescriptive guidance on personal conduct, friendship, cheerfulness, and agreeable behaviour in company, illustrated with anecdotes and moral examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Candour about one's own faults and achievements
rubrics_metrics.description: The candid Mind, by acknowledging and discarding its Faults, has Reason and Truth for the Foundation of all its Passions and Desires; a Man must lose his Consciousness before he can rejoice in any Falshood without inward Mortification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Admit mistakes rather than defend them; avoid taking more credit in the eye of the world than you deserve; confessing imperfections is not a diminution of greatness—obstinacy in the wrong is the mark of little minds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authentic attribution of honours
rubrics_metrics.description: There is nothing but what a Man really performs, can be an Honour to him; what he takes more than he ought in the Eye of the World, he loses in the Conviction of his own Heart.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not claim credit for others' accomplishments; public reputation should be grounded in genuine performance to avoid inward mortification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Greatness of spirit means acknowledging error, not obstinacy
rubrics_metrics.description: It is far from Greatness of Spirit to persist in the Wrong, nor is it a Diminution of Greatness of Spirit to have been in the Wrong: Perfection is not the Attribute of Man.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Value the capacity to admit error; imitating fortitude by obstinacy (including defending servants' faults) is a vice, not a virtue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preferential treatment of wounded veterans / civic gratitude
rubrics_metrics.description: I never make use of any body to row me, that has not either lost a Leg or an Arm. I would rather bate him a few Strokes of his Oar, than not employ an honest Man that has been wounded in the Queen's Service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In hire and public offices, give weight to those who served and were wounded in service; anecdotal example (Sir Roger) advocates employing and showing special regard for veterans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Civility in ordinary salutations
rubrics_metrics.description: My old Friend... his Custom of saluting every Body that passes by him with a Good-morrow or a Good-night... he cannot forbear this Exercise of Benevolence even in Town.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cultivate the habit of greeting people courteously in daily life; simple acts of civility make one popular among neighbours and neighbours alike.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generosity to the needy
rubrics_metrics.description: The Knight called a Waiter to him, and bid him carry the remainder to the Waterman that had but one Leg.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show small acts of charity (sharing food, gifts) toward the poor or disabled; concrete example given to illustrate moral worth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Religion must not be used to subvert civil liberties
rubrics_metrics.description: Christianity left us where it found us as to our Civil Rights... it is a most impious Blasphemy against that holy Religion, to father any thing upon it that might encourage Tyranny, Oppression, or Injustice in a Prince.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not claim that religious doctrine justifies removing civil liberties or encouraging tyranny; religion should not be invoked to endorse oppression.

rubrics_metrics.name: Friendship defined: mutual, habitual inclination to promote one another's good
rubrics_metrics.description: Friendship is a strong and habitual Inclination in two Persons to promote the Good and Happiness of one another.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Friendship requires both love and esteem; it is a cultivated, lasting disposition oriented toward another's welfare.

rubrics_metrics.name: Love and esteem are necessary foundations of friendship
rubrics_metrics.description: Love and Esteem are the first Principles of Friendship, which always is imperfect where either of these two is wanting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You cannot have full friendship if you love without esteem or esteem without affection; both affective and respectful regard are required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Friendship excludes envy
rubrics_metrics.description: Friendship immediately banishes Envy under all its Disguises. A Man who can once doubt whether he should rejoice in his Friends being happier than himself, may depend upon it that he is an utter Stranger to this Virtue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A true friend rejoices at a friend's prosperity; suspicion or resentment at a friend's happiness indicates absence of genuine friendship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer prudent, discreet friends to zealous or ostentatious ones
rubrics_metrics.description: A Friendship which makes the least noise, is very often most useful: for which reason I should prefer a prudent Friend to a zealous one.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Valuing quiet fidelity and usefulness over loud zeal; examples from Atticus/ancient models who served friends discreetly across parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Friendships may be formed between persons of different humours (complementarity)
rubrics_metrics.description: A Likeness of Inclinations in every Particular is so far from being requisite... that I believe we shall find some of the firmest Friendships to have been contracted between Persons of different Humours.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Difference of temperament can complement and supply defects; friendship does not require identical tastes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reproach from a friend should be just and sparing
rubrics_metrics.description: The Reproaches therefore of a Friend should always be strictly just, and not too frequent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When pointing out a friend's faults, ensure fairness and avoid constant censure which can wound or drive the friend away; advice should aim for the friend's advantage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary business of friendship: to inspire life and courage
rubrics_metrics.description: The proper Business of Friendship is to inspire Life and Courage; and a Soul thus supported, outdoes itself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Friends should encourage and strengthen one another; depriving a friend of such support causes them to droop.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duties to a friend are more voluntary and thus more blameworthy if violated
rubrics_metrics.description: We are in some measure more inexcusable if we violate our Duties to a Friend, than to a Relation: since the former arise from a voluntary Choice, the latter from a Necessity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because friendship is chosen, breaking its obligations is morally worse than failing family duties that are compelled by relation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not break with a worthy friend lightly
rubrics_metrics.description: It will doubtless hold much stronger with respect to a worthy one, that he may never be upbraided for having lost so valuable a Treasure which was once in his Possession.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preserve valuable friendships; ending a good friendship can be a lasting regret—treat friendship as a treasure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agreeableness in company should be natural, not artificial
rubrics_metrics.description: The true Art of being agreeable in Company... is to appear well pleased with those you are engaged with, and rather to seem well entertained, than to bring Entertainment to others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not adopt an affected manner to please; be genuinely pleased with the company and adaptable to its humour; apparent enjoyment is more valuable than forced display.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid monopolizing conversation with one's recent personal news or stock topics
rubrics_metrics.description: How unaccountable then must their Behaviour be, who... give themselves the Air of a Messenger, and make as distinct Relations of the Occurrences they last met with... you must hear how the Stocks go; ... tell you, Mrs. Such-a-one is charmingly handsome, because he just now saw her.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not interrupt a group's subject by insisting on telling only your recent events or gossip; be mindful not to derail others' enjoyment with self-centered reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wit without discretion makes a bad companion; avoid deriding others
rubrics_metrics.description: Witty Men are apt to imagine they are agreeable as such, and by that means grow the worst Companions imaginable; they deride the Absent or rally the Present in a wrong manner, not knowing that... you equally hurt him.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid humour that humiliates or singles people out; good company requires discretion, not merely clever sallies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adaptability: receive law from, not give it to, your company
rubrics_metrics.description: The Companion who is formed for such by Nature... gives to every Character of Life its due Regards... It must appear that you receive Law from, and not give it to your Company, to make you agreeable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be flexible to different groups' temperaments; do not try to dominate or impose your standards—conform sociably to the group's tone without affectation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cheerfulness promotes health and soothes the mind
rubrics_metrics.description: Chearfulness is, in the first place, the best Promoter of Health... Chearfulness bears the same friendly regard to the Mind as to the Body: It banishes all anxious Care and Discontent, sooths and composes the Passions, and keeps the Soul in a Perpetual Calm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cultivate cheerfulness as beneficial to both body and mind; it reduces anxiety and improves longevity and social ease.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appreciation of nature and proper aesthetic environments fosters cheerfulness
rubrics_metrics.description: If we consider the World in its Subserviency to Man... The Sun... has a particular Influence in chearing the Mind... Fountains, Lakes, and Rivers, are as refreshing to the Imagination as to the Soil.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seek out natural beauty—gardens, birds, green landscapes—to encourage cheerfulness; utilitarian and aesthetic values often coincide in nature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of colour (green) as a practical aid to cheerfulness and visual comfort
rubrics_metrics.description: The Poets ascribe to this particular Colour the Epithet of Chearful... All Colours that are more luminous, overpower... whereas the Rays that produce in us the Idea of Green... give the animal Spirits their proper Play.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical tip: green is soothing to the eye and invoked as pleasant by painters and poets; small environmental adjustments (e.g., green cloth) can ease the eye after intense visual work.
